evidence.note: CONFIRMED: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py registers claim_unavailable (verb claim.force) with predicate `_true`, so PO.apply auto-approves ANY claim.force while the standing window is open, regardless of the item's lease. Mechanism: _claim_by_approval (api/lifecycle/claim.py) re-runs a refused agent claim as claim.force -> operator_gate -> policy. Falsifier: a claim.force for an item with NO lease should NOT be answered policy:claim_unavailable. Pre-fix it WAS (operator_gate returned ok, stamp policy=claim_unavailable on a no-holder T1). Post-fix the predicate is _claim_unavailable = (it.lease is not None and not it.lease.live(time.time(), cfg.lease.grace_s)), which returns False for no-lease and live-lease, True only for a lapsed holder. Regression tests in tests/test_approvals_policy_claim.py; the existing window-behaviour test now gives T1 a lapsed lease to keep its intent.

Start with ddflow_brief + ddflow_recall 'claim_unavailable approves any claim.force'. Claim before edit (isolated worktree fix-B-claim-unavailable-fires-past-deps, as_agent high2). Work on the one shared file (policy.py) sequenced after merge-done landed high3's complete_unavailable fix (sha 423af9c97d5c). Regression test written to FAIL on the unfixed `_true` predicate and PASS post-fix. A reviewer from another model family is used (grok-4.7/gemini).

Replaced the claim_unavailable predicate in ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py: `_true` -> `_claim_unavailable(it, target, cfg)` returning `it.lease is not None and not it.lease.live(time.time(), cfg.lease.grace_s)` (imported time). It answers only a LAPSED holder lease; a no-lease item and a live-lease item are a person's call. Added tests/test_approvals_policy_claim.py (predicate boundary: no-lease False / live False / lapsed True; end-to-end claim.force on a no-holder item -> not auto-approved). Updated tests/test_approvals_policy.py::test_a_windowed_rule_stops... to give T1 a lapsed lease (holder gone, at 0.0, ttl 1) so the window-behaviour test keeps testing the window, not the no-holder refusal.

evidence.note: Hunted the narrowed predicate `_claim_unavailable` for a vacuous or over-narrowing edge: no off-by-one (Lease.live returns not expired_at and not expired(now,grace); expired() is (now-renewed_at) > ttl+grace, matching the claim site's own takeover check in ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py). No vacuous truth: no-lease -> lease is None -> False (never silently passes); live holder -> live() True -> not live -> False (a live holder is refused, so --force over a live lease is never auto-fired). No dropped config: cfg.lease.grace_s is the same knob the claim site reads, so the two cannot drift. No unavailable-as-clean: a lapsed lease records the held item, not a tool outcome.

Search by OPERATION: the lapsed-holder condition is the claim take-over predicate, not a new one -- ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py already checks it.lease.live(now, cfg.lease.grace_s) at the claim site, and the rule's predicate now mirrors that same Lease.live API (same grace knob) rather than re-deriving it. No duplicate standing rule (claim_unavailable is the single claim.force rule; the predicate change narrows its when, adds no second rule). No stray file: diff is policy.py + tests only.
